sights.address: 1 Bay Street, St. George Terminal, Staten Island, NY 10301
sights.w: Free 25-minute harbor crossing between Whitehall (Manhattan) and St. George, passing within view of the Statue of Liberty; runs 24 hours, no ticket needed.
sights.k: ferry, free, Statue of Liberty views

sights.n: Snug Harbor Cultural Center & Botanical Garden
sights.w: 83-acre campus of Greek Revival buildings, a Chinese Scholar's Garden, and botanical gardens on a former sailors' retirement home; grounds free dawn to dusk.
Living-history village and museum complex spanning 300 years of New York history, with restored houses and costumed interpreters; open Wednesday through Sunday afternoons.

sights.address: 210 New York Avenue, Fort Wadsworth, Staten Island, NY 10305
sights.w: One of America's oldest military sites, guarding the Narrows beneath the Verrazzano bridge; the tiered granite Battery Weed and Fort Tompkins offer sweeping harbor views. Part of Gateway National Recreation Area.
Victorian Gothic cottage on the shore that was home to pioneering photographer Alice Austen; now a museum of historic and contemporary photography with Narrows views.

sights.address: North Shore Waterfront Esplanade, Bank Street, St. George, Staten Island, NY 10301
sights.w: Two white sail-like forms framing the Manhattan skyline, honoring the 274 Staten Island residents lost in the September 11 attacks and 1993 bombing; each name inscribed on a granite plaque.
Gateway to the Staten Island Greenbelt, a 2,800-acre network of woodlands, wetlands, and marked hiking trails in the middle of the borough; center has exhibits and trail maps.

sights.address: 1000 Richmond Terrace, Building A, Staten Island, NY 10301
sights.w: New York City's only remaining general-interest museum, covering art, natural science, and local history; located on the Snug Harbor campus in St. George.
17th-century stone manor near the southernmost point in New York State, where a failed 1776 peace conference between the British and American delegates was held during the Revolution.

sights.n: Jacques Marchais Museum of Tibetan Art
sights.w: Stone temple-style buildings and terraced gardens housing one of the largest collections of Himalayan and Tibetan art in the U.S.; the Dalai Lama visited in 1991.

sights.address: 200 The Promenade at Lighthouse Point, Staten Island, NY 10301
sights.w: Museum on the grounds of the former U.S. Lighthouse Service depot beside the St. George ferry terminal, telling the history of American lighthouses and lightkeeping.
Compact West Brighton zoo known for its serpentarium and reptile collection, plus aquarium, big cats, and a children's farm; open daily with free Wednesday afternoons.
Wooded 90-acre preserve at the heart of the Greenbelt, laced with hiking trails, ponds, and boardwalks; a former Girl Scout camp turned nature sanctuary.

food.dish: Grandmothers' nightly Italian menu (rotating nonna specials)
food.w: Bib Gourmand trattoria near the St. George ferry where a rotating cast of grandmothers cook regional Italian and 'Nonnas of the World' menus that change nightly.

food.address: 524 Port Richmond Avenue, Staten Island, NY 10302
food.w: Blue-collar Port Richmond tavern serving thin, crackly-crust pizza since 1937 under the motto 'In crust we trust'; the plain cheese and garlic-onion white pies are the classics.
Family pizzeria running since 1960, famous for a paper-thin cracker crust and its vodka-sauce pie topped with fresh mozzarella and basil.
Cash-only Dongan Hills neighborhood tavern open since 1940, prized for a thin-crust white clam pie and old-school bar-pizza atmosphere.

food.dish: Weekend rice-and-curry buffet (black pork curry, devilled chicken)
food.w: Elaborately decorated Stapleton restaurant, among the first Sri Lankan spots in NYC, known for its weekend all-you-can-eat buffet of curries served on banana leaves.

food.dish: String hoppers with dhal and sambol
food.w: Tiny, cash-only Tompkinsville storefront in 'Little Sri Lanka' cooking homestyle rice-and-curry and string hoppers from a steam-table counter since the late 1990s.

food.address: 501 Port Richmond Avenue, Staten Island, NY 10302
food.w: The original 1928 Port Richmond stand, a summer institution serving scores of Italian-ice flavors plus cream-ice and ice-cream combinations from a walk-up window.
